name: French (Min)

rules.name: Preparing for the Minor
rules.desc:
To enroll in all French literature courses taught in French, students must pass first-year French [FRENLANG 1, 2, 3 or FRENLANG 1A, 2A] or complete the placement exam.
Additionally, students are highly encouraged to complete FRENLANG124 Advanced French: Composition, Writing, and Presentation or successfully tested above this level through the Language Center.

rules.name: Required Courses
rules.desc:
Complete at least 2 FRENCH courses for a total of at least 8 units. At least 1 of the required courses must be taken in the French language at the 100- or 200-level (FRENLANG 124 is the only language class that counts for this requirement).
Courses listed below are EXAMPLES and students are not restricted to this list. Students should refer to course descriptions to make sure the course is being taught in French the year they take it.

rules.name: Electives

children.name: FRENCH courses at the 100 or 200 level
French language courses at or above FRENLANG 21C (up to three, 12 units)
Approved courses elsewhere: other departments, Bing Overseas Paris, ESF (up to 10 units), SLE (up to 10 units), Digital Humanities (up to 5 units)

rules.desc:
• Coursework within the department. Additional FRENCH courses taught by French faculty (may be conducted in English or French) at the 100- or 200- level.

• Language coursework. Up to three language courses in French at or above FRENLANG 21C for a maximum of 12 units.

• Coursework in other departments relevant to the degree, with approval by the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

• Bing Overseas Study Program. Courses taken at the Bing Overseas Studies in Paris program with prior approval of the Director of Undergraduate Studies.

• Education as Self-Fashioning (ESF) courses taught at least partially by a French and Italian Department faculty member. Students may count a maximum of ten units.

• Structured Liberal Education. Students may count up to 10 units of SLE toward the major electives.

• Digital Humanities course. Student work must reflect French interests. Prior approval of the Director of Undergraduate Studies. Maximum of five units.

rules.name: One required course taught in French at the 100 or 200 level (or FRENLANG 124)

gpa: A grade point average (GPA) of 2.0 or better must be achieved in each course.
grading: All courses must be taken for a letter grade and passed with at least a ‘C’.
policies: These 24 units may not be used toward any other major or minor.
transferPolicy: External test (i.e. AP credit) and transfer credit are not accepted for the French minor.
reviewNotes: The audit checks the 24 units in at least six courses, two FRENCH courses (or FRENLANG 124) for at least 8 units, and electives from FRENCH courses at the 100 or 200 level or up to three French language courses at or above FRENLANG 21C (12 units at most). Every course must be letter graded with a C or better. You or the Director of Undergraduate Studies check that one required course was taught in French, and approve electives from other departments, Bing Overseas Paris, ESF, SLE or Digital Humanities, which you add by hand. AP and transfer credit do not count, and the 24 units may not also count toward another major or minor.
